| a01_single_node | All five loop stages run on one node in one Slurm job (no distributed selfplay, BUILD_DISTRIBUTED=0); stages share the node's GPUs via cudaDeviceToUse keys. | infrastructure | active | — | arxiv-1902.10565::synchronous_loop_smoke |
| a02_gpu_cap_start_at_1 | At most 4 GPUs total across all running jobs; the design runs one job on 1 GPU (b200 free 2/128, b300 0/8 on 2026-09-03; a 2-GPU request projected a multi-week wait) and adds GPUs only through async_multi_gpu_layout after measure_stage_throughput shows single-GPU saturation (duty > 70 %). | compute allocation | active | — | arxiv-1902.10565::selfplay_stage; arxiv-1902.10565::scale_up; arxiv-1902.10565::async_multi_gpu_layout |

| a04_b200_fallback | Partition preference for every chain link: b300 when, at the moment the link resubmits its successor, a b300 node has a free GPU and no RESERVED/DRAIN/DOWN/MAINT in its State=; otherwise the next candidate of KTG_PARTITIONS, tried in order, and when none has a free GPU the LAST candidate. The knob defaults to 'b300 b200' (so the fallback is b200, the historical behaviour this assumption was named for); the live production chain (job 301099 and its successors) carries KTG_PARTITIONS='b300 b200,l40s' (mission.json decisions[3], human 2026-09-04), so its fallback is the Slurm multi-partition set b200,l40s. The preference is evaluated at submission, up to one link length before the successor can start, and is not re-evaluated: a successor pinned to b300 waits for b300 (a03 covers the resume; this covers only where it queues). | partition | active | — | arxiv-1902.10565::env_build; arxiv-1902.10565::loop_resume_under_walltime; arxiv-1902.10565::selfplay_stage |

| a12_single_chain_per_basedir | Exactly one resubmit chain runs against a given BASEDIR at any time. The chain state files (.failcount, .chain_depth, .breaker_tripped, STOP, and since the third repair .cycles_completed, the progress counter the loop bumps after every completed cycle) and the per-BASEDIR retention pruning (scripts/dated archives, shuffleddata, selfplay generations via codes/data_budget/prune_retention.py --basedir) are not protected by a lock, so two concurrent chains on one BASEDIR would prune each other's archives and share one breaker count. Reproduced consequence for the counter (validator scenario S3, evidence/loop_resume/validation_repair3_harness.txt): when another writer advances .cycles_completed while a link's loop is failing, finalize() credits that progress to the failing link and clears its failure run (2 -> 1 instead of 2 -> 4), so a second chain on the same BASEDIR can keep this chain's breaker from ever tripping. | operations | active | — | arxiv-1902.10565::loop_resume_under_walltime; arxiv-1902.10565::data_budget |
